# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 16:56 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 199 active entries of tips_notebook.json (26 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But if a corroborated Lookout names X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, especially if X denied the visit or claims a role that doesn't fit. Don't acquit on the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat. (seen in 17 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone. (seen in 15 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips). Converging evidence is enough, so don't stall on 'what fact is disproved?'. If a Clerk may hold a rig, a passed nomination means death: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying. (seen in 15 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar. (seen in 12 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. A night's result never reaches your will if you die that night, and a Mortician can clean wills. (seen in 11 games)

## Village
- Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. Withheld results revealed later look retrofitted. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil (Good to a Seer) that night. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so post the caveat and rely on the vote ledger late. (seen in 15 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No on their nomination or cast Innocent votes that could have changed the outcome. A Guilty vote clears no one. Do the vote math: a hopeless Innocent proves little. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or steer loudly on Day 1; the leader-like voice dies first. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM. (seen in 15 games)
- PM clusters followed by shared nominations flag a likely bloc, but a PM link is a lead. A Jester or Executioner may create one on purpose. (seen in 16 games)
- Weigh premise contradictions above awkward wording. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff). If you must hang one, use a bare Guilty majority and keep key roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 15 games)
- A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. Keep SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool even after the Yakuza fall; a Not Evil result or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. (seen in 10 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily. The last unverified late 'Vanilla' is usually the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate (Yes and Guilty), but first check in night chat whether your Innocents plus a doubled vote can save them. Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester. (seen in 21 games)
- Fake-claim safely: assume the real holder counterclaims, an Accountant audits your tokens and exact-role checks test you. Never copy a just-flipped or publicly active role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 14 games)
- No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night. (seen in 13 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with an agreed cover story for the visit. Move it the same night a Lookout names the holder. (seen in 12 games)
- After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 11 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover. (seen in 8 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive a night attack, deny it or commit to one consistent claim. Switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely Katana targets. Post the full visitor list before the named players explain their visits, and point out that you named them first. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets. (seen in 14 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes). Use Basic shots, and remember a hidden Cardinal's death kills another villager. (seen in 9 games)

## Clerk
- Rig early on a Day when a Good player is the likely nominee; teammates vote Innocent. Never rig a Day a teammate may be nominated. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills. (seen in 4 games)

Carol's death on N3 meant I never had to rule on it, but I would not have known how. R8 says 'with two Yakuza alive, both must agree' but never says how the vote works with one Yakuza left. On N4 I treated Erin's choice alone as the majority. R20 step 5 says Yakuza learn each other's actions, but it does not say whether a lone surviving Yakuza still gets a summary. I folded it into Erin's own result.
answers.missing_information: I had no structured state panel and tracked everything by hand from the log: alive list and seat order, Katana holder (Erin all game), and token counts (Frank's 2 medic tokens, Bob's 2 swap tokens, Carol's spent archive token). Seat order was never shown explicitly; I only inferred it from the speaking order each Day. I also had no per-night visit table, which I needed to answer Lookout watches (Heidi->Frank on N2, Frank->Heidi on N3/N4) and to check whether a Sheriff result should be overridden. On N4 I had to remember myself that Erin held the Katana at the end of the night, so Heidi's check on her had to return Not Evil.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a one-line resolution summary per night: visits, attacks against defense, and appearance overrides applied. That would let me verify results before sending them, instead of reconstructing them. I also wanted to tag a player's [Claim] as stale or updated; Bob's Day 3 claim still said 'No Night 1 action or result'.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: On Day 5 Erin's claim and last will both came through as the literal string ':null'. That looks like an empty or failed field being serialized rather than a real will; it should show as 'no last will'. My own result formats were inconsistent: the N1 attack notice was merged into Alice's Lookout result, the N2 notice to Heidi was a separate message saying 'Last night' although it was sent during the night, N3 results dropped the 'Night N result:' prefix, and N4 merged the Yakuza summary into Erin's result. Frank publicly claimed Grace had sent private messages to Carol; it was actually Carol who messaged Grace. That was a player misread, not a system error.
answers.suggestions: Give the moderator a live state sheet: alive players in seat order, Katana holder, every token count, active traps/rigs/frames, and the current Jester/Executioner targets. summary: Village won cleanly because Frank's free Standard protection blocked the first two Katana attacks, on Alice on N1 and on Heidi on N2. That kept the Sheriff alive long enough to check Bob on N3, and Bob read Evil. Heidi posted the result first thing on Day 4, and Bob, a Smuggler claiming Vanilla, was hanged 5-2. The Yakuza lost through several errors. They kept attacking claimed investigators instead of the publicly claimed Medic. They never used Bob's two swap tokens. They left the Katana on Erin even after Bob was put on trial on Day 3, when giving it to Bob would have made Heidi's N3 check read Not Evil. Both Yakuza also claimed Vanilla, which overlapped with the real Vanilla, Dave, and fed Carol's suspicion. Erin then voted Innocent on Bob's hopeless trial and, on Day 5, made a fatal slip: she said that hanging her would leave only Village among the non-Jesters. Only the last Yakuza could know that. Village refused Grace's Jester self-nomination, so the Jester never got her win. Frank never protected himself despite having 2 tokens and died on N4, but by then the Yakuza were down to one player.

tips_feedback.why: Erin ignored this tip and voted Innocent on a 5-2 hang. That vote became the core of Dave's case against her, which shows the tip was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Medic: Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets.
tips_feedback.why: Free protection stopped the Katana on Alice and on Heidi. Frank ignored the self-protect and no-announce parts, and he died on N4 with tokens unused.

tips_feedback.tip: Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily. The last unverified late 'Vanilla' is usually the hidden Yakuza.
tips_feedback.why: Carol applied it before the slots were filled and overstated the math, saying two Vanilla claimers must be lying. She was rebutted and retracted, which discredited a suspicion that was actually correct and led to Bob's 0-8 acquittal.

issues.description: On Day 5 Erin's claim was logged as '[Claim] Erin: :null' and her revealed last will was ':null'. The harness seems to be printing a null or missing value as a literal string, both in the claim tracker and in the publicly revealed will. A player (Frank) also noticed it in the debrief.

R14 (stall rule) says everyone loses if a Day begins with no deaths in 'the three previous Nights and three previous Days', but it doesn't say what happens when fewer than three Days have occurred. Day 4 follows only Days 2 and 3, since there is no Day 1. Carol, Dave, Grace and Frank all said a quiet Night 3 would make everyone lose at Day 4; under a literal reading that may be wrong. The rule should say how missing Days count early in the game.

On Day 3 several players (Dave, Frank, Grace, Carol) repeatedly asked Heidi to post her 'Night 3' result, although Night 3 hadn't happened yet. Heidi had to point out that no N3 result could exist. This suggests confusion about phase numbering (no Day 1, Night N comes before Day N+1).

Carol misread the Archivist mechanics. She claimed the single Vanilla Villager entry in her archive capped how many Vanilla claims could be true, and that claimed roles 'take' real slots. The real entries are a random sample of 5 of the 7 players, and the rule text says this. She later retracted it, but it drove two trials. Also, during her own trial she said 'I'm voting Innocent on Bob', which shows confusion about which trial was in progress.

The Night 1 archive message to Carol said it shows '7 roles, one for each of the 7 other players', then said 2 are fake. The 'one for each player' wording contradicts the 5-real/2-fake structure and may have fed Carol's later slot-counting mistake.

The Medic's token wording ('Spend 1 token to give Strong Defense instead. Spend 1 more token to protect yourself instead') was reported as confusing in feedback. It is unclear on first read whether a Standard self-protection costs 1 token, and how the costs stack.
